title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative:
Kenya's economic growth has been driven by large-scale infrastructure projects, yet small businesses and the youth continue to face challenges in accessing meaningful employment. This disparity has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and the growing effects of climate change. The country’s development plans, under Vision 2030, emphasize the need to create sustainable jobs, improve labor relations, and strengthen social protection systems to address unemployment and underemployment, particularly among vulnerable groups.
This Country Programme Outcome (CPO) focuses on enhancing the capacity of workers' organizations, particularly the Central Organization of Trade Unions – Kenya (COTU-K), to engage in policy development and social dialogue that advances the rights and welfare of workers. By providing technical assistance to COTU-K and its affiliates, the ILO aims to strengthen their ability to advocate for labor rights, social protection, job creation, and environmental sustainability. This includes supporting COTU-K in its efforts to develop strategic advocacy papers on critical issues such as workers' rights, social protection, labor laws, and climate-induced migration.
The CPO also aims to support COTU-K in promoting the ratification of key International Labour Standards, including conventions on social protection, occupational safety, and migrant workers’ rights. Through these efforts, COTU-K will be better equipped to influence national policy, including the review of labor laws and the adoption of national employment policies that benefit workers and foster inclusive development.
In addition, the ILO’s support will enable COTU-K to address gender inequality and discrimination in the workplace, focusing on issues such as gender-based violence, disability inclusion, and labor migration.
